text:
andrea: Quick ping on PR #8421 — adds an allocator swap heuristic that reduced steady-state GPU memory by ~6% and increased throughput in our microbatch harness. Can I get 2 reviews? planning to canary tomorrow morning.

andrea: bench summary (microbatch, 8xA100, seq=1024):
```
master: throughput=2.1k tok/s, p95=52ms, p99=120ms
pr-8421: throughput=2.4k tok/s, p95=55ms, p99=140ms
mem: master=48GB, pr=45GB
```

andrea: net: +14% throughput, mem down, but tail p99 up ~16ms on longseq slices. not huge but visible. attaching raw artifacts: https://bench.redwood/refs/8421/artifacts

chris: thanks. can you paste the exact bench command you ran? want to reproduce locally quick.

andrea: sure —
```
run_bench --model redwood-v1 --seq 1024 --batch 16 --duration 300 --tag pr-8421
```

sam: do we know whether p99 bump correlates to certain request sizes? longseq only?

andrea: yeah looks like it appears mainly at seq >= 2048. microbatch config amplifies it because KV cache churn hits alloc path more.

benchbot: [automated note] additional CI microbench run finished: https://ci.redwood/bench/8421/2026-03-16 — baseline vs pr diff attached.

chris: can you run 2048 and 4096 quick? 2048 is our common tail case. if p99 delta there is bad we should canary with lower traffic.

andrea: running 2048 now, will post results in ~10m.

(andrea posts)
andrea: 2048 run results:
```
master: throughput=1.0k tok/s, p95=110ms, p99=260ms
pr-8421: throughput=1.15k tok/s, p95=118ms, p99=298ms
```

andrea: so p99 +38ms at 2048, throughput +15%.

tanvi: that tail bump could affect customer SLAs on long prompts. can we add a fallback rule in routing to route seq>=2048 to master until we fix?

mike: agree with tanvi. also would like to see a canary with 10% traffic and a rollback guard on p99 >= +30ms.

chris: I can review the allocator changes tonight. expect comments re: lock-free path and a micro-optim that might remove the tail. please don't merge until we get the fallback + guard. :thumbsup:

andrea: sounds good. I'll add a routing rule draft in the PR and a smoke test for the canary threshold.

sam: one more ask — can we get a heap/memprofile for the 2048 run? want to confirm it's allocation churn not fragmentation.

andrea: will grab it and upload.

(benchbot posts)
benchbot: microprofile uploaded: https://ci.redwood/profiles/8421/2048/heap.html

chris: quick skim — looks like a spike on the swap path during KV eviction. I'll leave detailed comments in PR.

andrea: thanks all. tagging @mike for the merge window decision — if we keep rollback guard and routing fallback, can we merge during Thurs morning window?

mike: Thurs morning sounds fine if we have the guard + a short canary (10m) and a manual rollback checklist.

andrea: will update PR with the guard logic and checklist. requesting 2nd review after I push the routing patch.

chris: on it — will review after you push.

sam: i'll +1 on perf impact analysis once memprofile shows churn.

andrea: pushed routing + guard change at https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/8421/files — ping when you can.

chris: reviewing now. small nits, but overall ok. leaving one suggestion on the hot path removal.

mike: once chris + sam approve, go ahead and schedule for Thurs AM canary. please put rollback playbook in the PR description.

andrea: thanks — will do. :rocket:
